thread:
sam: Heads up — noticed a batch of quantization eval runs didn't show up in the dashboard. artifacts uploaded but indexing step seems to have skipped them.

jules: saw the same, good catch. Was this the q4-8bit jobs?

sam: yep the q4 runs from yesterday. S3 objects present under s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/2026-03-19/, but ES index has no documents for those keys.

nina: any errors in the runner logs? I can tail the eval-runner pods.

sam: runner logs show a short stack but it's swallowed by the uploader: 
```
WARN uploader: missing index_key, skipping indexing for artifact 4f2e...
ERROR uploader: failed to send to indexer: 400 bad_request -> "null shard_key"
```

mike: ahhh we changed the metadata schema last week to add shard_key but didn't make it mandatory in the old runner path. New uploader expects shard_key or index_key, old traces don't have either.

jules: that explains duplicates too — some traces got re-ingested with random S3 object names, doubling storage.

olga: quick question — is shard_key the same as model + commit hash? Need deterministic value for indexing.

nina: current plan in the schema doc: shard_key = sha256(model_name + model_commit + eval_seed) % 128 (as string). But some older traces only had eval_id.

sam: two concrete problems: 1) missing indexing for ~1200 artifacts from yesterday, 2) CI flake where eval-runner unit test fails when metadata lacks shard_key — blocking a deploy.

ci-bot: CI build #2567 failed: tests/eval/uploader_test.py::test_indexing_without_shard_key — AssertionError

mike: for (2) easy fix: change unit test to assert uploader falls back to computing index_key from eval metadata instead of failing. But we should be explicit in code. PR ready?

jules: I'll open a small patch to compute fallback_index = sha256(concat(model,commit,seed)) and set that as shard_key if absent. Also add a metrics counter for "uploader.fallback_shard_key".

olga: +1. For (1) reindexing plan: we can run a one-off job to scan S3 prefix, compute fallback shard_key for each artifact without ES doc and bulk-index. But watch throttling.

nina: pagination note: the inventory of objects is ~1.4k, should be fine. But some objects are >10MB logs and the indexer chokes on the full_text field. Need to strip per-sample raw logs to a text_summary or move them to blobstore and only index the summary.

sam: here's a minimal example of current trace metadata that failed indexing: 
```json
{
  "artifact_id": "4f2e9a",
  "model": "gptx-3b-quant-q4",
  "commit": "a1b2c3d",
  "eval_seed": "42",
  "outputs": [ ... large array ... ],
  "full_text": "<20MB raw token log>",
  "uploader_version": "v0.12.0"
}
```

mike: indexer expects trimmed fields: `full_text_summary` capped at 4k chars, `artifact_key` as s3 path, `shard_key` string. Otherwise 400.

jules: new patch will: compute shard_key fallback, strip `full_text` to `full_text_summary` with first 4k chars, and add `artifact_key` before calling indexer. Also emit a warning log.

olga: let's be careful with PII — trimming full_text may still include PII. We should run a redaction step or at least flag these artifacts for manual review if they contain likely PII patterns. Add `pii_review`: true/false in metadata.

sam: good call. We can run a fast regex check for emails/ssn-like numbers and set pii_review. Mark that as non-blocking for indexing but flagged.

nina: operational plan: 
- jules opens PR with fallback + trimming + metric (GH#4891)
- mike runs one-off reindex job that computes fallback shard_key for s3 objects missing ES docs (script in tools/reindex_artifacts)
- schedule reindex job with rate limit 50/s and backoff for 429s
- olga and security review PII flagging implementation
- sam monitors dashboards and sets alert for "indexer.missing_docs > 0 for 10m"

jules: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4891 (draft). includes uploader unit test fix and integration test adding a large-log case.

ci-bot: CI build #2569 triggered for PR 4891. Current status: running tests.

mike: I'll prep the reindex job. Plan: use s3 inventory + lambda-ish worker to POST to indexer endpoint with computed payload. We'll add `dry_run=true` flag first and log what would be indexed.

olga: about retention: we discovered duplicates due to re-ingest; we should add dedup by artifact's content hash in the indexer. If artifact already has an artifact_hash in ES, skip. That avoids double billing.

sam: yes add `artifact_hash = sha256(s3_object_bytes)` and ES unique constraint on that field (or use upsert by artifact_hash).

nina: CI note: integration test should include a scenario where uploader_version is old and metadata missing shard_key — ensure fallback path exercised.

jules: agreed. I'll add test vectors and mock indexer responses for 400->success after fallback.

mike: timeline: PR -> tests -> merge -> deploy uploader patch today; reindex job tomorrow morning in low-traffic window.

olga: one more ask: update dashboard to show "artifact index lag" (delta between S3 object time and ES indexed time), and a monthly storage diff metric to catch duplicates.

sam: added ticket INC-2345 for dashboard + alerts.

nina: anything else?

sam: that's it. thanks all. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: automated note: reindex worker template saved as runbook/reindex_worker.md (editable).
